alex: Heads-up — after the FP8 rollout on the 40G cluster we started seeing 12–18% tail latency regressions on mid-size batches (seq_len 256–512). not constant but spikey.
maya: @alex can you paste the perf trace? :eyes:
alex: perf-bot posted a flame + kernel timeline. short summary: kernel selector picks FP8 fast-path for most shapes but falls back to an INT8-path for oddly padded shapes. fallback cost + extra memcpy seems to be the culprit.
perf-bot: Attached profile: cpu_time=12.3s, gpu_time=9.7s, kernel_switches=42, mem_copies=18

```
# kernel timeline snippet
0.00s conv_fp8_fast - 48%
0.11s attention_fp8 - 22%
0.25s attention_int8_fallback - 18%  <-- heavy tail
0.48s kv_update_memcpy - 12%
```

samir: Seeing the same on staging. looks correlated to batch packing when continuous batching groups short requests with medium-length ones leading to weird kernel shapes (M x K dims not aligned to tile size).
lee: Could be the kernel-shape constraint we added last month. that selector assumes pad-to-64 columns for FP8 kernels; if final packed width <64 it forces int8 path.
maya: That explains it. Workload distribution changed after PLG spike — more varied user prompts, more mix of seq lengths.
alex: Quick repro: run continuous-batcher with these inputs (mix of 64/300/512) and enable `RUNTIME_TRACE=1`

```
# repro command
./run_continuous_batcher --trace --mix 64,300,512 --batch-ttl-ms 20
```

samir: I dug into KV cache side-effects: when the fast-path is chosen we keep KV layout densely packed; fallback path reorders and issues an extra gather memcpy that invalidates prefix cache hits, so even later tokens pay
maya: Oof. So the perf hit is both kernel switch overhead + KV cache thrash. two levers.
lee: Proposed fixes:
- relax kernel-shape constraint: allow smaller widths with modified tile launcher
- add a fast check in selector to prefer stable path (avoid flip-flopping) for same batch composition
- make KV memcpy async and coalesce with next token step

alex: Ran a quick patch: selector hysteresis + coalesced async memcpy. microbench shows tail latency drops from 18% to ~3% on repro traces.
perf-bot: New profile attached: kernel_switches=8, mem_copies=4, gpu_time=8.4s

```
# new timeline
0.00s conv_fp8_fast - 62%
0.10s attention_fp8 - 28%
0.35s kv_update_async - 10%  <-- coalesced
```

maya: Nice. Any quality regressions from allowing smaller tile widths for FP8? we need calibration check.
samir: Did int8->fp8 shape test with calib set. no loss on our eval prompts (n=2k). but we should run the longer eval sweep.
lee: I'll schedule a nightly eval run with the quant-calibration harness. also flagging rollout gating for Dedicated customers.
alex: Also note: padding waste still matters. when continuous batching pads short requests to 512 to fit tile, even FP8 fast-path degrades throughput due to extra compute on padded tokens. we should prioritize packing heuristics that minimize pad area before changing kernels.
maya: Agreed — scheduler should prefer grouping similar seq lengths when latency SLOs allow. maybe add a soft-bin packer.
samir: Action items:
1) lee: land selector hysteresis + async memcpy (PR coming)
2) maya: run full quant-calib eval (2k prompts) and post results
3) alex: tweak batcher packer to reduce pad waste and run A/B
4) perf-bot: nightly regression alert if tail latency increases >5% after deploy

lee: PR draft: selector: add `preferred_path_stability=0.75` and `async_kvcopy=true` defaults. leaving knobbed flags so we can experiment.

```
# selector config snippet
{"preferred_path_stability":0.75, "allow_small_fp8_width": true, "async_kvcopy": true}
```

maya: If nightly eval passes, plan staged canary: 5% cluster -> 25% -> full. keep rollback metric: kernel_switches > baseline * 2 OR tail latency +5%.
alex: Sounds good. I'll monitor and post updates here.
perf-bot: Created incident ticket #INC-2027 for tracking perf regression gating.
lee: cc @ops to watch Dedicated fleets for unusual SLO adjustments.
maya: Thanks team — good catch. small selector heuristics + packer improvements seem to fix majority of regression without retraining quantization.
samir: Will follow up with calibration artifact logs if any pop up during the eval run.
alex: end of thread for now. :thumbsup:
